speaker: Mr Charles Chong
text: asked	the Minister for National Development what measures the Ministry intends to take to better safeguard public monies and residents' service and conservancy payments to Town Councils and to recover any improper past payments made by Aljunied-Hougang Town Council (AHTC), especially in light of the July 2016 KPMG report on AHTC's financial controls and systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To recap, AHTC had received qualified financial statements from its own independent auditors for four consecutive financial years (FYs) since FY2011.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AHTC's auditors were unable to determine the accuracy of the Town Council's various balances, expenses and receivables, including those relating to their service and conservancy charges (S&CC).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: There were also other audit observations, including late Sinking Fund transfers, incorrect usage of Sinking Funds, as well as inadequate disclosure and segregation of duties over related party transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When AGO undertook a special audit on the Town Council in 2014, it similarly found lapses in the Town Council's management of Sinking Funds, governance of related party transactions, management of S&CC arrears, internal controls and procurement, as well as inadequacies in their record management and accounting system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: When AGO's report was debated in Parliament in February last year, the Town Council's then-Chairman and her fellow Town Councillors assured us that they had "already taken concrete steps to address and remedy many of the issues".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: More than a year has passed but the Town Council appears to have made little progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: KPMG had noted in its July 2016 report that only a few of the remediation steps that AHTC had said they would do had been completed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: While AHTC had indicated that they aimed to complete the remediation works in 15 months, that is, starting from July 2016, KPMG estimates that at the Page: 7 current rate of progress, the remediation process will take at least 18 months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Instead of completing the remediation plans expeditiously, what we have seen from the Town Council in this past one and a half years is a series of actions that have only slowed down, prolonged and frustrated the whole process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, the Town Council attempted to avoid having one of the Big Four firms appointed as its independent accountant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Town Council also rejected the joint appointment of accountant with Pasir Ris-Punggol Town Council (PRPTC) to review AHTC's past payments in relation to Punggol East (PE), and when PRPTC appointed its own accountant, the Town Council refused to grant access to documents or to attend the coordination meetings called by the Housing and Development Board (HDB) with all parties to try to resolve the impasse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This pattern of behaviour is all the more worrying when set against what KPMG had stated in its July 2016 report, that the remediation of the control failures will require that the Town Councillors engage to "reset the tone at the top of AHTC, emphasising competence and accountability".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Apart from AHTC's slow progress in remedying the control failures, MND is also concerned with various systemic control failures that KPMG's latest report has highlighted, including: First, the extensive use of manual journal entries that bypassed AHTC's accounts payable module, for payments totalling more than $60 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: KPMG has flagged this as "highly irregular" and "makes effective oversight of payments by the Finance Department practically impossible".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, temporary clearing accounts which were not investigated or cleared, containing transactions amounting to over $648,000 in total.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, the use of dummy codes which might not update payee records in the Accounting System, for transactions amounting to over $270,000 in total.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These control failures continue to paint a serious state of affairs in AHTC and are a cause for concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: KPMG noted that these control failures could conceal duplicate, fictitious or fraudulent payments, which could have been made without being detected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: As ordered by the Court of Appeal, KPMG is currently reviewing the past payments made by the Town Council to ascertain whether any were improperly made and, therefore, ought to be recovered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The findings are due on 31 August 2016, the end of this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: MND asked AHTC to cooperate fully with the accountants to carry out a thorough and robust review of the past payments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The matter has dragged on for many years, with multiple Court hearings and not much actual progress made.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For four FYs consecutively, AHTC has not had accounts that passed accountants' muster.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This is accurately summed up by the Auditor-General in his report that "there was no assurance that the accounts are accurate or reliable, or that public funds had been properly spent, accounted for or managed".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Residents of Aljunied, Hougang and also Punggol East need to be assured as to whether or not there were any improper past payments that ought to be recovered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Singaporean public also needs to know as public monies and grants are at stake.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Page: 8 MND and HDB will be studying the accountants' subsequent findings carefully and will take the necessary and appropriate actions to ensure that residents' interests are safeguarded and that any improper past payments are duly recovered.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Minister for National Development had said that MND will be reviewing the Town Councils Act.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State tell us when this review will be completed and if MND would consider including it in the Act penalties for wilful acts of concealment or non-cooperation with MND, HDB or other agencies which result in MND, HDB or other agencies being unable to detect or assess financial transactions which may be of public interest, or of non-compliance with the Act?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Will the Minister also consider including in the Town Councils Act provisions to enable MND, HDB or other agencies to compel Town Councils and their contractors to provide records in the event of non-cooperation by Town Councils or their agents in connection with investigations into the affairs of Town Councils?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that sense, we will look at the Member's suggestions in the course of this review.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think I have addressed the Member's questions.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given that MND is doing a review of the Town Councils Act, would MND consider setting a reasonable timeframe and deadline for the preparation and submission of audited financial statements or distribution of assets and liabilities after each political boundary change?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is certainly something that we need to look at in the course of this review.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State confirm if the joint appointment of accountants was required by the Court of Appeals in CA114 of 2015, or HDB had included it as a prayer to the Court of Appeal at any point in time?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This AHPETC no longer exists in its Page: 9 previous form as a legal entity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Instead, because of the intervening General Elections, Punggol East was carved out and handed over to PRPTC and became part of that entity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, based on the Town Council's declaration order, we are advised that this means that all the rights, obligations and liabilities of Punggol East then flow on to its successor organisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that sense, the accounts that relate to AHPETC are in relation to what would now be AHTC, which is one successor, and PRPTC, which is the other successor in respect of the Punggol East portion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The orders then need to be applied to all the entities for which the issues of AGO and all the Foo Kon Tan reports, and, indeed, the nub of the discussion in Parliament, they all relate to the former AHPETC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that sense, both were required to comply with the Court order, which was initially at AHPETC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are given to understand that PRPTC wanted to discuss the issue of appointment because they wanted to have some coordination and efficiency because, essentially, they are looking not just at PE or AHTC but looking at the whole previous entity and how they inter-relate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are also given to understand that there was an attempt to then appoint a joint accountant but without success.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In order to assist in Members' understanding of the question that the Member asked, allow me to take this House and Members through what we understand had happened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: AGC had highlighted the importance of appointing accountants that could competently execute the duties envisaged by the Court of Appeal's orders, given the complexity of the work entailed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB suggested that the accountant be from the Big Four accounting firms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And to avoid duplication of effort, competing access to documents and incurring of costs, HDB also asked both Town Councils to consider making a joint appointment of accountants.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And that is the genesis of the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On 4 December 2015, AHTC, however, nominated Business Assurance, while PRPTC sought to jointly appoint PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) with AHTC on 15 December 2015.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When asked to reconsider its nomination, AHTC had applied to the Court of Appeal for directions on the issue of appointment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: AHTC also did not respond to HDB's subsequent queries on Business Assurance's experience and expertise, for example, their years of experience in the relevant areas of audit and the latest Practice Monitoring Programme (PMP) inspection results.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Court of Appeal later directed AHTC to file an affidavit to respond to HDB's queries by 11 January 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the day of the deadline, AHTC had filed the response but instead of answering HDB's questions on Business Assurance's experience and competence, AHTC said that Business Assurance had withdrawn due to "intense media scrutiny", that since Business Assurance had withdrawn, it was no longer necessary to provide the information on Business Assurance and that the Town Council had nominated a new firm, MRI Moores Rowland, instead.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the night of 19 January 2016, the night before the next Court of Appeal hearing, AHTC wrote to the Court to state that MRI Moores Rowland had also withdrawn on 17 January 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this was 19 January; the date they had withdrawn was on 17 January.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The latest development was also not mentioned in AHTC's two affidavits by the Chairman, I believe, on 18 January 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the Court of Appeal hearing on 20 January 2016, it emerged that Business Assurance withdrew because it did not want to reveal its PMP inspection findings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This led the Court of Appeal to raise concerns about whether the Court had been apprised of all the facts in a candid and forthright manner and whether the Town Council had in place a system to ensure due diligence in selecting candidates to do this work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is where I come from, as background, to the response to the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On 1 March 2016, AHTC then announced that they have appointed KPMG LLP with HDB's consent ‒ HDB consented because it is one of the Big Four ‒ to perform the task ordered by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After KPMG's appointment was announced by AHTC, PRPTC informed HDB on 3 March 2016 that it wished to appoint KPMG jointly with AHTC, but later updated HDB that AHTC was not agreeable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was in this context that HDB agreed to PRPTC's appointment of a different set of accountants, namely, PwC to carry out its Court of Appeal orders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To ensure that the reviews were carried out efficiently and effectively, HDB invited both Town Councils and both sets of auditors to a meeting in June to discuss the implementation details, such as scope and timeline, but AHTC twice declined to attend as it did not agree that PRPTC was bound by the Court of Appeal order, precisely what the Member has asked earlier in relation to PE.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: AHTC also did not give PRPTC access to the documents of PE and requested that HDB seek clarification from the Court of Appeal first.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, that matter is really in one sense, in a way, sub judice as well.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And at the last hearing, PRPTC did not attend, so we were not able to move further on that matter.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Next, I would just like to clarify also Mr Charles Chong's question to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am not sure whether Mr Charles Chong is accusing AHTC of wilful concealment of any documents.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We appreciate all this attention on us and how bad we are.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But in order for us to get a proper perspective, is MND saying that the auditors of the other Town Councils have not picked up control failures in the other Town Councils since MND is receiving these annual management letters as the regulatory Ministry?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have not seen such an email for the years that I had been —

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether this email was actually prompted by the KPMG report and a concern by the Ministry that perhaps other Town Councils also need to get themselves better organised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the second question, the email which sent some slides, basically, it flows from the concerns that have arisen with regard to the AHTC and AHPETC issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We wanted to send out information to make sure that all Town Councils, not just AHTC, were on the same footing and would have this information, especially since we are on a new term, after the General Elections.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for the Member's first question about whether the other Town Councils have control failures, well, all the Town Councils ‒ and I believe AHTC, too ‒ should be submitting their annual accounts by the end of this month, and once everything is in order, they will be tabled before Parliament and then all Town Councils, I believe, will put it on their websites.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the auditors' findings would then be made available, and the Town Council Management Report (TCMR) would then, of course, come out in due course to set out the banding as well as the findings on corporate governance and other issues relating to Town Council governance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member says that other Town Councils may also have governance failures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have no doubt that, from time to time, they will make errors as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These will be picked up and the MND and HDB secretariats will raise them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will appear in the TCMR and we will speak about them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think it is also important for this House to keep in mind the context of the issues that AHTC had been facing, in that this is not KPMG citing control findings in relation an audit arising from a year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Instead, actually, this whole issue started when the new AHTC had taken over from 2011 from a Town Council which hitherto did not seem to have any of these qualified accounts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for the last four financial years, this is a public statutory body charged with municipal services and Page: 12 collecting millions of dollars in public revenues and receiving millions of dollars in grants from taxpayers every year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, collecting money every month through its principal source of revenue, which is S&CC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And its accounts have not been seen fit by accountants to be passed without disclaimers and without qualification.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I think this is accountant-speak, but accountants will say that a qualified set of accounts is a serious matter.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Not by any accountant, but by accountants appointed by AHPETC and then AHTC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: FY2011/2012, four consecutive years, until the present date.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: AGO is the independent accounting body which audits Government agencies as well, and there were lots of questions that were raised yesterday on Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that, in sum, is not about one individual process or one individual matter, but it is a finding of the AGO on the whole system of AHPETC and its accounts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In Parliament, this was also debated and all Members were involved deeply in the discussion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members from AHPETC had, on the surface, agreed with the Motion and we all know that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But in substance, it did not seem that there were real answers in the debate and some of the questions asked were not answered.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Be that as it may, this matter then went to two levels of the Supreme Court, both at the High Court and the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And again, serious findings were found after lawyers from both sides provided affidavits and addressed the Court.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It also stated that there were numerous breaches of the Town Councils' Act and regulations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The High Court found that it was the "height of financial irresponsibility" and if the Town Council were an entity under the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act (BMSMA), like a condominium, running a condominium, there would be serious ramifications both in civil and possibly in criminal law.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was a "travesty", the Court said, to ignore its duties, and that some parties who were before the Court had not been completely truthful.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That was actually in the High Court's orders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Similarly, the Court of Appeal made certain findings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, it repeated what the High Court had found.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have just spoken about 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In relation to what the KPMG auditors are doing in relation to limb two – which is checking whether there are improper past payments – we came across an article by the Chairman of the Town Council, Mr Pritam Singh, to Lianhe Wanbao one or two weeks ago where he said, translated, "We have to rectify the issues raised, the AGO's report and audit all the previous transactions with the former managing agent FM Solutions and Services Pte Ltd (FMSS).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If unlawful transactions are confirmed, as Town Council Chairman, I have a responsibility to recover that money with my team." Looking at the KPMG's remit, looking at what the Town Council is setting out to do and what the Chairman has articulated publicly to the newspaper, could the Chairman perhaps, in the spirit Page: 13 of this discussion, confirm that he cannot now rule out illegality or unlawful transactions?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The word I used was not "unlawful", but "improper", and that word really follows in concert with the Court of Appeal's judgment which was to look at improper past payments, so it will be how KPMG puts it out in its past payment review report.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second issue I would like to raise is the point that the Senior Minister of State brought up about the joint appointment of accountants which HDB, if I heard him correctly, agreed with PRPTC on 3 March.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am a bit surprised that the joint appointment of accountants is so important now because HDB did not raise it to the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The issue of joint appointment, like I have said earlier, is water under the bridge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It would have been ideal if both could address one set of accountants because, really, it is one former entity and one set of accounts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In relation to the entire estate of the different precincts that used to form AHPETC, that is why HDB has suggested, after the Court of Appeal had ruled, that AHPETC had to appoint an accountant, and then suggested that perhaps both sides could consider.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And that is in the context that the suggestion was made.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Coming back to the Member's confirmation, and I thank him for confirming that he meant "improper" as opposed to "unlawful", because that could be a translation issue.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can the Senior Minister of State confirm which individual made that statement?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I just want to remind Members that we have had a very lengthy extensive debate on this issue not so long ago.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We do not want to restart that debate again because the issues concerned are broader issues.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, just a clarification and then we are moving on to the next question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is in the context of the General Election rallies being made.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think these statements can be easily found as a matter of Page: 14 public record.
